Have you ever had the pleasure of embarking on a journey that takes you through a landscape of limitless imagination and adventure? A journey that tantalizes the senses to the point that you find yourself with pages full of scribbles, adorned with drawings and doodles that may only make sense to you?

For me, that journey began with the opening lines of Harry Potter and birthed an entire universe that encompassed everything from wizarding schools to dragons and mythical creatures. I'm not alone in my love for reading, but I dare to say there are some things that capture our hearts more than others do. Why does that make me happy? It brings meaning to our days, as if we are part of an enormous family, enjoying a potluck dinner of words and pictures, an eat-your-hearts-out meal specially prepared for us as readers.

This potluck, however, is varied and diverse, and I fear we would soon become exhausted by a singular flavor. So, why do we love books so much? The answer would somehow stretch over multiple lines, as long as there exist literates. However, my sentiment gravitates towards the idea of escape. Escaping from the drudgery of daily life. Escaping + enjoying. It's as if we soar on the wings of imagination and emerge on the other side of the story with a reservoir of enthusiasm and freshness.

Before I share some of my favorite books from different ages and genres, let me take you with me on a journey, weaving the tales of my beloved books that have changed the course of my life and graced it with memories that I hold dear to my heart.

My first real introduction to the enchanting world of books was when I received "Harry Potter and The Philosopher's Stone." It's more than just a book. It's an experience, a magical journey through a world brimming with wonder, where every person, creature, and stone you step on carries the possibility of enchantment. As I turned the pages, I found myself transported to a world I never thought possible. It was the beginning of my love affair with books that would extend further than Harry's wand and Baggins' hearth talk.

"Where the Wild Things Are" gave me the courage to be just as wild and free as the creatures on the pages. The story of Max, a little boy who must deal with his anger and fears, was a journey through emotions that transcended generations. King receives an emphatic salute for his brilliant narrative voice in this classic tale.

"1984" shone a light on the world's importance - where we stand, who we are, and the course we're walking. Or perhaps, if we're not careful, where we'll exclude ourselves. A more recent favorite, "The Hunger Games" thrust me into a world where my love for all things fantastical and beyond my reach soared to new heights. It is far more than a simple story of revenge and survival - it's a story about the protection of oneself, the preservation of freedom and the enemies that can creep up if we are not guardian enough.

"The Alchemist" opened my eyes to the beauty of dreams and the hunger for one's own path. There's science in it, art in it, and the fundamental urge to make of our lives our own masterpiece. If we have the courage and willingness to follow our hearts, directed us by fate or the universe, we will gradually understand exactly what arouses that external call.

"To Kill a Mockingbird," quite the classic, took us through an era of change and destruction, where injustice and hatred were markings on American history, markings that Blakey Wiles paints both in stunning detail and with all the impact of a bull in a china shop. But it's an impact that reshapes said china shop, as it helps readers learn how kindness can conquer the most stubborn darkness if not oppressive and not resisted.

Among the classics, one book left my heart wide open, wider than a Mexican wedding cake. "The Midnight Library" by Matt Haig provides an inspiring message that we are all connected and, with the right mindset, can remake our lives. This book opened new doors for me. Known for its unique, otherworldly tale, it's not merely a book but a journey that claims our wingback togas and opened our eyes to how little, or instead, how much, we may have taken for granted.

If you ask what sets apart these books from the plethora of others read, then the answer stumbles upon the words, experiences and emotions that each book invokes, uniquely encapsulated by the minds of their respective authors. They are equal parts mirrors and windows, showcasing our world while giving the reader an opportunity to see through someone else's eyes.

Don't be afraid to explore new worlds - likes and dislikes vehicles of knowledge. Differences do not draw lines but are instead sources of beauty. Books, after all, have the capability to inspire, entertain, educate, and bind us, much like the shared laughter and conversations around a warm dinner or a board game. As you turn the final page, ask yourself, "How does this make me feel, and what can I take with me to enrich my life?"

This is not spending time with books. This is time well spent.
